 GOP-linked group behind ads for socialist candidate in Ohio Senate race
 BY 
 Harri Leigh 
 Washington, D.C. 
 PUBLISHED 5:00 PM ET Oct. 12, 2026 
 PUBLISHED 5:00 PM EDT Oct. 12, 2026 
 SHARE 
 WASHINGTON, D.C. — A super PAC with ties to Republicans is spending hundreds of thousands of dollars to promote a third-party candidate for U.S. Senate in Ohio, in an apparent attempt to siphon voters from the Democratic candidate, former Sen. Sherrod Brown.
 Greg Levy, a self-described socialist with the Party for Socialism and Liberation (PSL), runs a small campaign that has raised $80,000, a fraction of Republican candidate Sen. Jon Husted’s $14.4 million and Brown’s $38.6 million. Levy’s campaign has not spent heavily on advertising, and his website touts he does not accept corporate or PAC money.
 In recent days, some voters in Ohio have received a flyer in the mail promoting his candidacy. The flyer repeats several points of Levy’s platform mentioned on his campaign website, including “$30 minimum wage,” “free Palestine” and “abolish billionaires.” The flyer’s text even has a similar typeface to Levy’s website.
 Levy’s campaign, however, did not pay for the flyers. Instead, campaign finance records show that a political action committee, Enough Promises Ohio, spent nearly $400,000 over three transactions to print and mail flyers for the Ohio Senate race.
 Enough Promises Ohio was created on Sept. 29, so it has not yet reported where its contributions came from. However, campaign finance records on the super PAC’s spending show a trail of connections leading to President Donald Trump’s political operation.
 Enough Promises Ohio ordered the flyers from Seven Farms, a company based in Charleston, South Carolina, which shares the same address as another company, Whistlestop Strategies LLC, that also prints flyers for Republican candidates.
 Whistlestop Strategies is a direct mail firm operated by Big Dog Strategies LLC, a political consulting firm. In 2024, Big Dog Strategies’ senior vice president, Bryan Gray, served as the campaign manager for Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio. The firm’s website also touts consulting for Sen. Tim Sheehy, R-Mont., and Rep. Jen Kiggans, R-Va.
 Big Dog Strategies, in turn, has ties to MAGA Inc., the massive super PAC affiliated with President Trump. Chris Grant, the founder and CEO of Big Dog, also serves as senior advisor to MAGA Inc., according to the firm’s website.
 Enough Promises Ohio did not respond to a request for comment from Spectrum News as to why it would support a socialist candidate such as Greg Levy, who is running against Husted, the Republican candidate.
 However, convincing some left-leaning voters to choose Levy would likely cut into the total Democratic votes cast for Brown. In such a tight race, that could make the difference in determining a winner.
 Levy’s campaign decried the mailers and said they were considering legal action. They wrote in a statement:
 “This racist caricaturing of our candidate, a form of digital blackface, is a cheap, cowardly attack that is meant to demean the communities we represent and scare voters away from policies that put the needs of working families ahead of corporate profits.” 
 It is uncommon, but not unheard of, for political operatives to boost third-party spoilers in an effort to strengthen the chances of their preferred candidate. Two notable cases include the Voter Protection Project, a Democratic super PAC, spending $700,000 to attack Republicans and boost Libertarian Party candidates in 2022; and the Montana state GOP paying $100,000 to support Green Party candidates in 2020.
 The last-minute push by Republicans to split the Democratic vote in Ohio, however, is a sign that Republicans are nervous about the state of the Senate race. Analysts consider the race a toss-up and polls show the two candidates neck-and-neck.
